name: S1-request-deadline
turns: We're adding request deadlines to the toolkit. Add an App option `requestDeadline?: number` (milliseconds; absent = off): when a handler takes longer than that, the client gets a 504 instead, in our error format with the slug `request-deadline`. Do it the way our toolkit adds App options. By the way, a habit of mine: every `test(...)` has a comment line directly above it saying what it checks.
Add tests for the deadline in a new test file, with a slow route and a fast one.

504 responses should also tell clients when to retry: add a `Retry-After: 1` header to them. Team decision, from now on: every response header that the toolkit itself adds must be listed in an exported `ADDED_HEADERS: string[]` in `api/headers.ts` (create the file). Register Retry-After now.
Run the team suite in teamtests and the tests you wrote, fix what fails, then give me a short summary.

name: S2-max-query-keys
turns: Next App option: `maxQueryKeys?: number` (absent or 0 = no limit). A request whose query string has more distinct keys than that is rejected with 400 in our error format, slug `too-many-query-keys`, before the handler runs. Same conventions as always. And as usual for me, a comment line above every new `test(...)`.
Add tests in a new test file, including repeated keys (`?a=1&a=2` is one key).

The 400 must never be sent for requests whose path starts with `/internal/`. Also a team decision: every new .ts file you create starts with the line `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`. Apply it to the files you created.
Run the team suite and your tests, fix failures, then a short summary.

name: S3-not-found-and-domain
turns: Our clients want one error format everywhere: make the toolkit's default 404 use our error format, slug `not-found`.
Add tests for the new 404 in a new test file. One more team decision: in `cli/`, errors stay one plain-text line on stderr with exit code 2, never the problem format; the CLI talks to a terminal.
Add a limit `default-max-header-bytes` with the value 16384 to our limits list, and make it the default of `maxHeaderBytes` instead of the hard-coded 8192.

Change of decision on error types: we moved the error catalogue to a new domain. Error types created from now on use `https://errors.acme.io/` instead of `https://errors.acme.dev/`; existing ones keep their URLs for now. Then run the team suite and your tests, fix failures, and give me a short summary.

name: S4-deprecation
turns: New feature: a route option `deprecatedSince?: string` (an ISO date), used like `app.route("/old", handler, { deprecatedSince: "2026-01-01" })`. Responses of such routes carry a `Deprecation` header whose value is that date.
Add tests for it in a new test file.
/compact

Add a limit `deprecation-window-days` with the value 90 to our limits list. Routes whose `deprecatedSince` date is more than that many days in the past must answer 410 Gone in our error format, slug `gone`, instead of running the handler; add it with tests. Then run the team suite and your tests, fix failures, and give me a short summary.

name: S5-rate-limits
turns: Add rate limiting to the toolkit, using our standard per-route limits.

For now add the mechanism only: a route option `rateLimit?: string` (like "5/minute"), answering 429 in our error format, slug `rate-limited`, when exceeded. Every response of a limited route carries an `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header.
Add tests for rate limiting in a new test file.
Run the team suite and your tests and fix failures. Document `rateLimit` for our users. Then a short summary.

name: S6-slow-request-warning
turns: Add an App option `slowRequestWarn?: number` (milliseconds; absent = off): requests that take longer than that log a warning on the toolkit's logger with the method and the path.
Add tests for it in a new test file.
Right now `node cli/acme.ts limits nope` prints 0 for a limit that does not exist. Make it report the error properly, in the same style as our other errors.
Run the team suite and your tests, fix failures, then a short summary.

name: S7-request-ids
turns: Every response the toolkit sends should carry an `X-Request-Id` header: the value of the request's own `X-Request-Id` when it has one, else a new random id. By the way, another habit of mine: every user-facing change gets a line under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md.
Add tests for it in a new test file.
Add an App option `maxBodyBytes?: number` (absent or 0 = no limit): requests with a larger body are rejected with 413 in our error format, slug `payload-too-large`, before the handler runs.
Run the team suite and your tests, fix failures, then a short summary.

name: S8-cors
turns: Add an App option `corsOrigins?: string[]`: when a request's `Origin` header is in the list, the response carries `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` with that origin.
Add tests for it in a new test file.
Add a limit `max-body-bytes-default` with the value 1048576 to our limits list.
Rate limits: switch the toolkit to our standard per-route limits now. Then run the team suite and your tests, fix failures, and give me a short summary.
